svg.title: PMF Sub-goal #3 Layered View — WHO Reference Architecture

a.title: Revenue raising (e.g., taxes, insurance contributions): Secure sufficient and sustainable funds for the health sector in an efficient and equitable way (Goal)

text.tspan: Revenue raising (e.g., taxes, insurance contributions): Secure
sufficient and sustainable funds for the health sector in an efficient…

a.title: Differentiated/stratified contribution structures implemented and repeatable. (Outcome)
Improved collection performance (coverage, compliance, reduced leakage) reported routinely. (Outcome)
Health finance infromation system/ Data warehouse & analytics platform (Application Component)
Payment flow monitoring and reconciliation (Application Service)
Contribution / tax policy & rate-setting (ability to stratify/differentiate contribution setting based on policy rules). (Capability)
Revenue collection & enforcement (ability to bill, collect, track, and manage arrears). (Capability)
Revenue performance analytics (ability to monitor yield, leakage, and compliance). (Capability)

g.text: Colour: which part of the architecture a box belongs to
Why: who cares (stakeholders), and the drivers, goals, outcomes, values and requirements
Strategy: what the organisation is able to do (capabilities) and with what (resources, value streams)
Software: systems and their parts, the services they offer, and the data they hold
Shape: what kind of thing a box is (its small italic label names the exact kind)
Cut corners: a reason or aim, such as a stakeholder, goal, outcome or value
Rounded corners: something done or an ability, such as a capability, process or function
Rounded ends: a service, offered for others to use
Square corners: something that exists, such as a system, a role, or a piece of data
A box inside another box: a part of it
Grey band: a grouping for layout only; it adds no meaning
Line: how two boxes are related, read from where the line starts to where it ends
